statement: Lola has $7$ identical marbles and three boxes colored red, blue and green. She puts all $7$ marbles into the boxes so that every box holds an odd number of marbles. In how many different ways can she do this?

choices.misconception: I found the two groups 1, 1, 5 and 1, 3, 3, but forgot that the boxes are different colors, so which box gets which amount matters.
I gave each of the groups 1, 1, 5 and 1, 3, 3 all 6 orders, forgetting that swapping two equal amounts gives the same filling.
I only made sure every box got at least one marble and counted 15 ways, forgetting that each amount must be odd.
I counted every way to split 7 marbles among 3 boxes, 36 ways with empty boxes allowed, and never used the odd rule.

hints: Which odd numbers can three boxes hold if they add to $7$?
List the possible amounts as groups without order first, then count how many ways each group can be placed in the three different boxes.
The groups are $\{1, 1, 5\}$ and $\{1, 3, 3\}$. Each has two equal numbers, so each can be placed in $3$ ways (choose the box that gets the odd one out).

solutions.reliable: Each box holds at least $1$ marble, and the amounts are odd numbers adding to $7$. The largest amount is at most $5$. The possible groups are $\{1, 1, 5\}$ and $\{1, 3, 3\}$. For $\{1, 1, 5\}$, choose which box gets $5$: $3$ ways. For $\{1, 3, 3\}$, choose which box gets $1$: $3$ ways. In all there are $3 + 3 = 6$ ways.
solutions.elegant: Put $1$ marble in each box. The other $4$ marbles must go in pairs to keep every amount odd, so Lola places $2$ identical pairs into $3$ boxes: both pairs in one box ($3$ ways) or in two different boxes ($3$ ways), $6$ in all.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
